rule: Fair-island generator: decide players per island from the start mode, derive three island masses from land budget, grow one island (blob plus compact phase, sea ring around start islands), copy it to each start with random mirror or quarter-turn, check every copy before any write, retry the whole map with masses shrunk 1 percent per failure, and fall back to the island generator when attempts run out. Start selection: score tiles by food, shield and trade plus half the best improvement, keep local peaks, restrict to starter flags, sample random tiles against a quality bar, relax the bar 5 percent per failed round, and gate each candidate by a walk-area flood fill, a hut rule, a temperature rule and a spacing rule. Biomes: quotas as shares of unmountained land, placed by a macro that moves a failed count to an alternate biome; terrain choice is a weighted draw on per-terrain property percents from the ruleset.
keep: copy one island with random symmetry, so starts look alike without being identical
check every copy before writing any tile (all-or-nothing placement)
bounded retry with a small per-failure shrink of the target, then a fallback generator
start value from what a tile produces, keeping only local peaks
quality bar relaxed by a fixed ratio per failed round, with a hard stop
walk-area flood fill with early exit as a start validator
terrain as a row with percent properties and flags, drawn by weight
change: split spacing from quality: the donor divides the spacing by the quality bar, so relaxing quality also relaxes spacing
replace nation and team allowances with our own zone or character allowances
keep biome quotas in zone family rows, not in five hard-coded calls
forbid a class of tiles by name (edge of the world) rather than by a temperature class test
look_test: Six 2-player zones from six seeds, shown twice side by side: one template copied with random mirror or quarter-turn, and free random placement. Dom judges which pairs look like two fair starts and whether the copies read as a place or as a stamp.
